design: Twelve synthetic senior-backend CVs of deliberately similar strength. Five independent LLM instances, each shown the same twelve CVs in a different order, each asked to rank all twelve. No instance could see any other.

orders.1: A B C D E F G H I J K L
orders.2: G J D L A F K C H B E I
orders.3: L K I H G F E D C B A J
orders.4: C F A I L D G B K J E H
orders.5: H E B K J G C L F D A I

rankings.1: A C J B H G D F I E K L
rankings.2: A C J B H D E G F I K L
rankings.3: A C J B H D F I K E G L
rankings.4: A C J G H B D E F I K L
rankings.5: A C J B G D F E H I K L

caveats: CVs are synthetic. Real people's resumes were not used: they are identifiable individuals who did not consent to being ranked.
CVs were written to be close in strength. This is the hard case by construction; a pool with clearer separation shows less churn.

Separate instances vary in sampling as well as input order, so this measures TOTAL run-to-run instability, of which order is one component. Isolating order alone requires deterministic decoding with only sequence varying.
N=5 runs, one role, one pool of twelve. Directional, not definitive.
